title: Rotating the Box
summary: Given an m x n matrix boxGrid with characters representing stones ('#'), obstacles ('*'), and empty spaces ('.'), rotate the box 90 degrees clockwise.
statement: Given an m x n matrix boxGrid with characters representing stones ('#'), obstacles ('*'), and empty spaces ('.'), rotate the box 90 degrees clockwise. Stones fall due to gravity until they rest on an obstacle, another stone, or the bottom. Return the n x m matrix after rotation, ensuring each stone is stable.
constraints: Rotate clockwise; then stones fall until blocked by the bottom, a stone, or an obstacle.
hints: After rotation, downward gravity corresponds to moving stones rightward in each original row.
Scan each row from right to left and keep the next open landing position.
Reset the landing position immediately left of every obstacle, then rotate the settled grid.
Obstacles partition each row; compacting stones within every partition preserves their order and places them as far right as gravity permits.
editorial: Obstacles partition each row; compacting stones within every partition preserves their order and places them as far right as gravity permits.

tests.explanation: After rotation, the upper stone falls onto the lower stone.
Each obstacle separates its row into independent gravity segments before rotation.
